answer: Escrowed reputation depreciation: each identity posts a small refundable deposit, but its usable reputation decays on a schedule tied to a network-wide activity nadir, so dormant sockpuppets lose standing before they can be sold. Every action emits a signed pulse that raises the identity's minimum required deposit; the marginal cost per extra identity therefore climbs steeply with each one created in a window. A fraudster must fund hundreds of deposits and keep every puppet active enough to stay above the violet threshold line, converting a one-time gate into a recurring, rising bill.
